name: @projexlight/sdk-lineage
summary: Cross-pool data-lineage projector (G8 closer): captures every transformation node + edge across the platform, projects them into a queryable graph, and backfills new pool families on attach. Answers 'where did this number come from?' and 'if we shred this source, what derivatives die?' Foundation for analytics audit + the SemanticPolicy + DSAR fan-out integrity guarantee.

events.name: lineage.node.recorded.v1
events.description: New lineage node committed (source, transform, or sink).

events.name: lineage.projection.completed.v1
events.description: Projector pass finished for a pool; carries node/edge counts processed.

models.description: Per-node row: kind (source/transform/sink), uri, schema_hash, owner_sdk, pool_index.
Per-edge row: from_node, to_node, transform_kind, transform_metadata.
Pending projections to apply when a pool comes online or its schema changes.
Per-(pool, node-kind) checkpoint so resumed backfills don't re-process committed work.

hooks.name: recordNode
hooks.description: Universal entry — every SDK that produces or consumes a data artifact registers the node.

hooks.name: recordEdge
hooks.description: Register an edge between two nodes after a transformation.

hooks.name: queryUpstream
hooks.description: Walk the graph backwards from a sink: what sources contributed?

hooks.name: queryDownstream
hooks.description: Walk forward from a source: what derivatives exist?

hooks.name: startProjector
hooks.description: Background worker that pulls inbox messages + projects lineage rows. Cross-pool aware (G8).

hooks.name: backfillPool
hooks.description: Backfill lineage for a newly attached pool; idempotent on the checkpoint.

scenarios.title: Rollup-spec produces lineage automatically
scenarios.when_to_use: Universal pattern. Every analytics rollup emits a node for the rollup target + edges from every source table. Documented here so SDK authors know what to call.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Lineage graph reflects every source → target derivation. Future queryUpstream on the rollup answers 'where did this number come from' in O(graph depth).

scenarios.title: Operator traces a suspicious KPI back to source
scenarios.when_to_use: Sev-3 ticket — 'this number looks wrong.' Walk upstream from the KPI node to every source table contribution.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns the upstream graph slice. Operator can spot the offending source table + identify the bug + write a backfill.

scenarios.title: What dies if we shred this source?
scenarios.when_to_use: GDPR right-to-erasure planning. Before shredding a source dataset, walk downstream to find every derivative that depends on it.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns the downstream subgraph. Operator knows which materializations need recomputation post-shred.

scenarios.title: Projector pulls lineage from a new pool family on attach
scenarios.when_to_use: G8 closer — when a new pool family attaches, the projector backfills its lineage so cross-pool queries see complete provenance.
scenarios.example_code:
import { backfillPool } from '@projexlight/sdk-lineage';
await backfillPool({ pool_index: 'pool-new-x', checkpoint_resume: true });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Lineage graph extended to include the new pool. Emits lineage.backfill.completed.v1 with the node/edge counts. Idempotent — re-running resumes from the checkpoint.

scenarios.title: vault.key.shredded.v1 propagates as lineage tombstones
scenarios.when_to_use: When a vault key is shredded, every node encrypted under it becomes effectively dead. Lineage marks those nodes tombstoned so downstream queries surface the dead-end explicitly.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Tombstoned nodes retain their position in the graph but mark themselves undecryptable. Downstream queries see the dead-end + can attribute downstream staleness to the shred event.

compliance_posture.notes: Lineage is the GDPR Art-22 + EU AI Act lever — for any automated decision or AI output, you can trace its inputs back to source. SOX data-quality controls satisfied by lineage + the materialized rollup audit. Cross-pool projection is the integrity guarantee on federated analytics queries.
